about.title: Apple Valley Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Apple Valley sits high in San Bernardino County, and its wide desert roads carry more traffic than the town's quiet character suggests. In 2025, the most recent final crash year, public records show 207 injury collisions here, with 326 people hurt and 11 lives lost. Bear Valley Road, Route 18, Apple Valley Road and Kiowa Road account for the largest share of reported collisions, and the numbers tend to climb on Wednesdays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m. as commuters head home. Behind each of those counts is someone dealing with pain, missed work and a phone that keeps ringing with calls from an adjuster. We handle car accident claims in Apple Valley on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. You describe what happened, and our team takes it from there.

whyChoose.title: Why Apple Valley Drivers Choose Us

items.title: Deadlines That Are Easy to Miss
items.desc: California gives most car accident victims two years to file, but a claim involving a city, county or state vehicle or roadway can require notice in as little as six months. We can pin down which clock applies to you before it runs out.

items.title: Partial Fault Does Not Close the Door
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you share some blame; your compensation is simply reduced by your percentage. California also places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and lost enjoyment of life in an ordinary car crash case.

items.title: Protecting Your Claim From Day One
items.desc: The other driver's insurer may ask for a recorded statement early, and you are not required to give one. We work on contingency and can step in to preserve photos, witness details and repair records while you focus on healing.

items.question: I was hit near the Bear Valley Road and Apple Valley Road area. Does where the crash happened matter?
items.answer: It can. Those corridors see some of the highest collision counts in Apple Valley, so nearby businesses and passing drivers may have camera footage or firsthand accounts that fade quickly. If the crash involved a government vehicle or a claimed roadway defect, the shorter six-month notice window against a public entity may also come into play. We can sort out those questions early.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company keeps calling for a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You do not have to, and most attorneys advise against it. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can shrink your claim later, even when you answer honestly. It is reasonable to say you will respond once you have spoken with a lawyer, and then contact us to discuss your case.

items.question: How much does it cost to speak with an attorney about my case?
items.answer: Nothing. We provide a free case review. We handle car accident cases on contingency, so our fee comes only from a recovery, and if there is no recovery there is no fee.
